name: tight-70s-warm
description: De-harshed variant of tight-70s-dry. Empirical isolation showed the hi-mid edge came from the Neve 1073's mf +2 dB @ 3.2 kHz (+ hf shelf), NOT the tape — so the Neve EQ is neutralized to mid 0 / air 0 (keeps only the low warmth + 80 Hz HPF + its transformer color) and the Studer A800 supplies the warmth (it measurably DARKENS: centroid -341 on this bus). Same Neve 1073 -> dbx 160 -> Studer A800 chain, gentle tape (input +6, 15 IPS, 456) for a low-end head-bump without upper-mid harshness. Apply to the measured-balanced, transient-punched dry bus. Built 2026-05-31.
intended_for: a dry, measured-balanced, transient-punched drum bus — when tight-70s-dry read too bright/harsh in the 2-5 kHz hi-mid
notes: mf_gain 0 + hf_gain 0 removes the 3.2 kHz harshness the isolation probe pinned on the Neve; the tape (not the EQ) provides 70s warmth. If too dull, add hf_gain ~0.5 (12 kHz air, above the harsh band) rather than re-boosting the mid.
